title: HTML5 & CSS3
summary: Nine skills cover almost every HTML/CSS ticket a junior front-end developer gets. Learn these deeply; look everything else up on demand.

skip.why: replaced by Flexbox and Grid (floats survive only for wrapping text around an image)
use tables only for tabular data
defer until after Week 6; native CSS now has variables and nesting, and frameworks are easy once fundamentals click
memorise patterns (centering, sticky footer, card grid); look properties up

modules.title: Semantic HTML that ships
modules.goal: Write a valid, accessible page skeleton from memory in under 2 minutes.
learn: The boilerplate: <!DOCTYPE html>, <html lang="en">, <meta charset>, <meta name="viewport">, <title>, linking a stylesheet
Landmarks: header, nav, main, section, article, aside, footer — and when a plain div is fine (styling hooks only)
One h1 per page; headings in order (h1 → h2 → h3). Never pick a heading for its size — CSS handles size
Text and lists: p, ul/ol/li, strong, em
Links: relative vs absolute paths, jumping to a section with href="#id"
Images: meaningful alt text (alt="" for decorative ones), width/height to prevent layout shift, loading="lazy"
button vs a: buttons do things, links go places — a favourite interview question
Tables only for tabular data: thead, tbody, th scope="col"

build.title: Your résumé in pure HTML (no CSS yet)
checklist: Header with your name and a nav of in-page links (About, Skills, Experience, Contact)
Skills as a list; each job or project as an article inside a section
Education as a small data table; contact links (mailto:, LinkedIn, GitHub)
Push to a GitHub repo

doneWhen: The W3C validator shows 0 errors, and the page makes sense with CSS switched off.

modules.title: CSS core: the cascade and the box
modules.goal: Predict which rule wins and why an element is the size it is — before you open DevTools.
learn: Selectors: type, class, descendant, child (>), grouping; pseudo-classes :hover, :focus-visible, :nth-child(); pseudo-elements ::before/::after. Style with classes, never IDs
The cascade: specificity is scored ID – CLASS – TYPE and compared left to right; on a tie the last rule wins. Avoid !important
Inheritance: text properties (color, font) inherit; box properties (margin, border) don't
Box model: content → padding → border → margin; set box-sizing: border-box on everything; know that vertical margins collapse
Units: rem for font sizes and spacing, % for widths, px for borders, ch for readable text width (max-width: 65ch)
Typography: font stacks, Google Fonts, line-height: 1.5, font-weight
Colour and decoration: hex, rgb(), hsl(), background, border-radius, box-shadow
display: block, inline, inline-block, none
A modern CSS reset as your starting file
DevTools: inspect, toggle declarations, the box-model diagram, and :hov to force hover and focus states

build.title: Style your Week 1 résumé
checklist: Add the reset, then a type scale in rem (body, h1, h2, h3)
Pick 1 font pair and a 3–4 colour palette
Turn each section into a card (padding, border-radius, shadow)
Visible hover and :focus-visible states on every link

doneWhen: No inline styles, no ID selectors in your CSS, and you can explain in DevTools why each overridden rule lost.

modules.title: Flexbox and positioning
modules.goal: Build any navbar, card row or centred hero without Googling.
learn: display: flex, main axis vs cross axis, flex-direction
The four properties you'll use daily: justify-content, align-items, gap, flex-wrap
Item sizing: flex: 1 to fill space, flex-shrink: 0 to stop squashing, and the min-width: 0 fix for overflowing text

Five patterns to memorise: Centre anything (display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center); Navbar: logo left, links right; Equal-height card row that wraps; Sticky footer: body as a flex column, main { flex: 1 }; Media object: image beside text
Positioning: relative + absolute for badges and overlays, sticky for headers, fixed for a back-to-top button
z-index only works on positioned elements and on flex or grid items

build.title: A product landing page
checklist: Sticky header: logo left, nav links right
Hero: headline and button beside an image, vertically centred
A row of 4 feature cards that wraps on narrow screens
A call-to-action banner and a footer that sticks to the bottom on short pages
A "New" badge absolutely positioned on one card

doneWhen: Zero floats, no fixed pixel widths on containers, and nothing breaks as you drag the window from 1440px to 800px.

modules.title: Grid and responsive design
modules.goal: One codebase that looks right from a 320px phone to a 1440px monitor, with 2–3 breakpoints at most.
learn: display: grid, grid-template-columns, the fr unit, repeat(), gap
The one-liner used everywhere: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)) — responsive cards with no media queries
grid-template-areas for page shells (header, sidebar, main, footer); spanning with grid-column: span 2
Flexbox vs Grid rule of thumb: Flexbox when content decides the size (one direction); Grid when the layout decides (two directions)
Mobile-first: write base styles for phones, then add columns with @media (min-width: 48em)
Fluid type without breakpoints: font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1rem + 3vw, 3rem)
Responsive images: max-width: 100%; height: auto, object-fit: cover for cropped thumbnails; know srcset and <picture> exist
Testing: DevTools device toolbar at 320, 768, 1024 and 1440px

build.title: Make it responsive
checklist: Rebuild your Week 3 landing page mobile-first so it works from 320px to 1440px
New page: a blog or portfolio home with grid-template-areas (header, sidebar, main, footer) that collapses to one column on phones
An auto-fit card gallery with cropped, same-size thumbnails

doneWhen: No horizontal scrollbar at 320px, at most 3 media queries per page, and headings scale smoothly as you resize.

modules.title: Forms, accessibility, modern CSS, deployment
modules.goal: Ship pages that work for keyboard and screen-reader users, adapt to dark mode, and live on a public URL.
learn: Forms: every input gets a <label for>; the right type (email, tel, number, date, password); textarea, select, fieldset + legend for radio groups; <button type="submit">
Native validation with zero JavaScript: required, minlength, pattern; style errors with :user-invalid; add autocomplete values

Accessibility essentials: Tab through every page — everything clickable must be reachable and show a visible focus ring; Never remove outlines without replacing them (:focus-visible); Text contrast at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text); Native elements first; ARIA only when no HTML element does the job
Custom properties: put design tokens (colours, spacing, radius) in :root; get dark mode by redefining them inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
Motion: transition on transform and opacity for hover effects, a simple @keyframes, and turn it off under prefers-reduced-motion
Organising CSS: reset → tokens → base → layout → components; BEM-style names (.card, .card__title, .card--featured)
Deploy: git add / commit / push, then GitHub Pages

build.title: Contact form + dark mode + go live
checklist: A contact page with name, email, phone, a topic select, a radio group and a message; all native validation
Move your résumé's colours into custom properties and add dark mode
Add hover/focus transitions that switch off with reduced motion
Deploy all builds from Weeks 1–5 to GitHub Pages

doneWhen: The form works with the keyboard alone, Lighthouse Accessibility scores 95+, and dark mode follows your OS setting.

modules.title: Capstone: a multi-page business website
modules.goal: Build and deploy a 3-page, fully responsive website for a fictional coworking space (invent the name, e.g. "Northdesk").

build.title: Multi-page business website
build.brief: Build and deploy a 3-page, fully responsive website for a fictional coworking space (invent the name, e.g. "Northdesk"). It's the exact kind of site agencies and freelance clients pay for, and it exercises every skill above — with zero JavaScript.
checklist: Home: Sticky header; nav that sits in a row on desktop and wraps or stacks on phones; Hero with a clamp() fluid headline and a call-to-action button; Amenities: an auto-fit Grid of 6 icon cards (no media queries); Location section: address, opening hours, map image with proper alt

Plans & Pricing: 3 pricing cards in Flexbox; the featured plan uses a modifier class (.plan--featured); An accessible comparison <table> with th scope; FAQ built with native <details>/<summary> — an accordion with no JavaScript
Book a Tour: Form: name, email, phone, date, plan (select), team size (number), message; Native validation and :user-invalid error styling; every field labelled

Site-wide: design tokens in :root and a dark theme via prefers-color-scheme; hover and focus transitions that respect prefers-reduced-motion; images sized with width/height, loading="lazy" below the fold; semantic landmarks and one h1 on every page

doneWhen: W3C validator: 0 errors on all 3 pages
Lighthouse (mobile): Accessibility 95+, Best Practices 95+, SEO 90+, Performance 90+
No horizontal scroll at 320px; checked at 320, 768, 1024 and 1440px
Every page fully usable with the keyboard, with a visible focus ring
Text contrast 4.5:1+ in both light and dark themes
No !important, no ID selectors, no inline styles
Live on GitHub Pages; README with the live link, mobile + desktop screenshots, and 3 things you learned
